meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-14 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Evan Brooks (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marta Li (Umbrage CTO), Connor Hale (Umbrage Platform Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Umbrage Head of ML)
summary: Discovery focused on time-to-first-token (TTFT) via PLG quicklaunch credits vs a reserved Dedicated pilot. Customer has strict PII handling and timeline aiming for Q1. They want baseline latency/cost tradeoffs and clarity on VPC/on-prem options and KMS. Next: pilot pricing, security docs, benchmark session.
topics: Use cases and success criteria (search rerank + chat support)
TTFT: quicklaunch credits vs reserved Dedicated pilot
Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, data residency
Benchmarks: latency targets and payload characteristics
transcript:
[00:00] Evan Brooks: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Evan from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Priya, our SE. Quick intro?
[00:12] Marta Li: Hi, Marta here. CTO at Umbrage Commerce. We've been exploring ways to add conversational product search and an internal reranker for merchant support.
[00:22] Connor Hale: Connor, platform eng. I'm responsible for infra and security gating.
[00:28] Sofia Ruiz: Sofia, head of ML. I'll lead the evaluation and benchmarking.
[00:34] Evan Brooks: Great. High level, we want to understand your constraints — timeline, data sensitivity, traffic patterns — and then outline options: quicklaunch (self-serve credits) to get TTFT down, or a Dedicated/reserved pilot for predictable throughput and isolation.
[00:50] Marta Li: Our main thing is PII — order numbers, emails — some of our merchant support flows include sensitive customer text. We also have a Q1 goal to ship an MVP of conversational search.
[01:04] Priya Desai: Thanks. For PII, we usually recommend either the hosted path with strict retention + no-logs for certain tiers, or a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for full control. Dedicated is in-between: reserved capacity with stronger isolation but still managed.
[01:20] Sofia Ruiz: Can you clarify the 'no-logs' on hosted? Is that a legal guarantee?
[01:25] Priya Desai: It's operational — certain plans don't retain request logs beyond ephemeral buffers, and we provide contractual terms. For full compliance where you need customer-managed keys, we suggest Private with KMS/HSM support.
[01:39] Connor Hale: Ok. Network-wise we can do VPC peering but not route through public IPs for production. Is VPC peering supported on the dedicated offering?
[01:48] Evan Brooks: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and a private endpoint. Private deployment is the only route that removes redwood-managed control plane access entirely for air-gapped scenarios.
[01:58] Marta Li: Cost is a factor. Quicklaunch credits are attractive because we want to prototype without long commitments. But if we get good traffic, reserved makes sense. How do you help us estimate when to move?
[02:10] Priya Desai: We provide profiling guidance: token cost models, and we can run a short benchmark that simulates your sequence length distribution. Typically we look at average token per request, RPS, and 95th percentile latency. We can recommend batching, caching, and quantization profiles to hit cost targets.
[02:28] Sofia Ruiz: For our reranker, sequence lengths vary — short query + embedding (100 tokens) then candidate contexts (avg 600 tokens). We care about 95th latency under 400ms for the chat layer.
[02:40] Evan Brooks: That's helpful. For 400ms P95, we often recommend a Dedicated profile with GPU-backed instances tuned for your model — or a hosted variant on a smaller seq length with aggressive batching. We'll need sample payloads to simulate.
[02:52] Marta Li: Timeline-wise: we want to decide by late November and start a pilot in December if feasible. Is that realistic?
[02:59] Evan Brooks: Yes — with quicklaunch credits you can be live in hours for basic endpoints. For a reserved Dedicated pilot, procurement + capacity might take a couple weeks but we can fast-path a two-week pilot if you give us payloads and test accounts.
[03:12] Connor Hale: Procurement headaches — do you have a standard pilot SOW or terms?
[03:16] Evan Brooks: We have a pilot agreement template and an expedited track for pilots under our PLG program; I'll send that after the call.
[03:22] Priya Desai: Quick note on data flows: if you want VPC-only, Dedicated supports egress controls. Private supports customer-managed KMS and full audit trails.
[03:33] Sofia Ruiz: Regarding models — can Redwood host our fine-tuned model or do we need to bring it via S3?
[03:39] Priya Desai: You can bring a custom model artifact. For hosted, we verify compatibility and performance; for Dedicated/Private, you can run your containerized runtime or our runtime with your model. There may be different quantization/compat settings to consider.
[03:54] Marta Li: Security checklist: SOC2, SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC, audit logs, KMS. Which of those are supported in hosted immediately?
[04:05] Priya Desai: Hosted has SOC2, SSO via SAML, RBAC on the console, and logs. KMS for hosted is limited to our managed key — customer-managed KMS is available on Private and in some Dedicated contracts. We'll share a matrix.
[04:17] Connor Hale: Can you show us the retention settings? We need logs purged or not stored by default.
[04:22] Evan Brooks: We'll send the retention policies and a whitepaper. For quicklaunch, default is short-term ephemeral retention unless a paid tier is chosen.
[04:31] Sofia Ruiz: Benchmarks — how do you do token accounting for embedding + rerank flows? I'd like to see end-to-end RPS cost.
[04:39] Priya Desai: We'll run a synthetic benchmark with your payloads: measure tokens per request, tokens per second, latency distribution, and cost per 1k requests under different configs (hosted small model, hosted larger, dedicated with batching).
[04:52] Marta Li: We also have a strict SLA expectation for some routes — chat support needs higher availability. Do you offer route-level SLAs?
[05:00] Evan Brooks: We have per-route monitoring and SLA options for Dedicated customers. Hosted has best-effort SLAs and uptime transparency; Dedicated/reserved comes with contractual SLAs for latency and uptime.
[05:11] Connor Hale: One blocker for us could be auditability. We need tamper-evident logs for model input/output for a subset of routes. Is that possible?
[05:19] Priya Desai: With Private deployments we can ship logs to your SIEM or S3 using signed, immutable objects. Dedicated can push to your log collector via secure channels as well.
[05:31] Evan Brooks: Quick aside — competitors? Are you evaluating others?
[05:35] Marta Li: Yes, we're also trialing Anthropic and seeing if OpenAI offerings fit our cost/latency. We're evaluating ModelServe for on-prem capabilities.
[05:43] Evan Brooks: Got it. We'll aim to highlight where Redwood gives predictable economics and simpler transition from quicklaunch to reserved.
[05:51] Sofia Ruiz: Practical question: what's the TTFT for a developer to call the API with a service key? In our experience it's often a day for SDK integration.
[05:59] Evan Brooks: For the quicklaunch self-serve flow, developers can be calling the API within an hour — create account, get credits, hit endpoint using SDK. For a more integrated flow with VPC peering and SSO it takes longer — usually days to a couple weeks depending on network approvals.
[06:14] Connor Hale: We will likely do internal devs on quicklaunch, but production must be either Dedicated or Private.
[06:19] Evan Brooks: Makes sense — common path. Start self-serve for TTFT and iterate to Dedicated as traffic ramps.
[06:26] Marta Li: Any guardrails to prevent data leakage during self-serve?
[06:30] Priya Desai: Yes: retention controls, masking helpers, and endpoint-level controls. We also provide a sandbox mode that strips or hashes PII for prototyping.
[06:41] Sofia Ruiz: For the reranker, we may want KV cache locality to reduce repeated context costs. Is that exposed?
[06:48] Priya Desai: We expose KV cache and prefix caching options — also batching controls. On Dedicated you get finer-grained control over cache size and eviction.
[06:57] Evan Brooks: If we run a benchmark next week, what are the must-haves from your side?
[07:02] Sofia Ruiz: Example payloads, expected RPS, success metrics (latency P95 target 400ms, cost target $X per 1k requests), and the subset of routes that will carry PII.
[07:14] Connor Hale: Also any IP allowlist for sandbox endpoints and a contact for infra troubleshooting.
[07:18] Marta Li: On procurement, who signs the pilot SOW? Do we need enterprise legal review for the quick pilot?
[07:24] Evan Brooks: For small pilot credits, usually a simple acceptance of terms works. For Dedicated pilot with reserved capacity, we provide a pilot SOW and can accommodate expedited review cycles.
[07:34] Priya Desai: I'll attach a sample SOW and our pilot terms after this call.
[07:39] Marta Li: How will model updates be handled for Dedicated? We need to pin versions during canary.
[07:44] Evan Brooks: You can pin model versions per route and use canary rollouts; Redwood Console supports A/B and rollback policies. We'll show that in a demo if you'd like.
[07:55] Sofia Ruiz: We will want to run a regression test on quality after quantization. Any tooling?
[08:01] Priya Desai: We have an Optimize toolkit: quality monitoring with prompt sets and regression alerts. It can run against canaries and prod and notify on deviations.
[08:11] Connor Hale: For billing, is there an itemized breakdown per token and model? Need that for finance.
[08:16] Evan Brooks: Yes, the console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route and per-model. We'll include sample billing spreadsheets in the follow-up.
[08:26] Marta Li: Let's talk about a concrete pilot shape: two-week bench — simulate 50 RPS with mixed embedding + chat traffic, one reserved route for chat with higher priority.
[08:36] Evan Brooks: That works. Our recommended pilot: week 1 profiling with sample payloads on hosted quicklaunch; if results meet performance gaps, week 2 move to a reserved Dedicated slice for comparison. That gives you both TTFT and production isolation data.
[08:50] Sofia Ruiz: I like that. For the hosted profiling, do you provide synthetic tokens vs running against our real data?
[08:56] Priya Desai: We can run either; many customers give anonymized payloads or masked PII. We can also run replay tests in our sandbox.
[09:06] Connor Hale: For the dedicated slice, do we need a commitment? Or can it be a temporary reservation?
[09:11] Evan Brooks: We offer pilot reserved capacity without a long-term commitment for trial customers; we call it a pilot reservation. If you convert to a full reserved contract we roll pilot credits into the commitment.
[09:25] Marta Li: Any blockers on encryption at rest for logs?
[09:29] Priya Desai: Hosted logs are encrypted with our managed keys. Customer-managed KMS is available in Private and select Dedicated agreements.
[09:36] Sofia Ruiz: Ok — we should be able to provide payloads by Thursday and want a benchmark by next Thursday.
[09:42] Evan Brooks: Great. We'll tentatively block time for a 60-minute benchmark session. Priya will coordinate.
[09:48] Marta Li: Onboarding docs — do you have a developer quickstart for embedding + chat?
[09:53] Evan Brooks: Yes — we have SDKs, quickstart templates, and Postman collections. I'll include a direct link in the follow-up.
[09:59] Sofia Ruiz: One more question: are you able to run on specific GPU types if we need low latency?
[10:05] Priya Desai: Yes, Dedicated gives control over instance families; Private lets you run on your choice of hardware. We'll profile on A100 vs H100 equivalents to see P95 differences.
[10:16] Connor Hale: For observability, how granular are traces? We need per-token timing where possible.
[10:21] Evan Brooks: We export traces, per-token timing breakdowns, and tokenization stats. Console shows token-level latency and cost attribution.
[10:30] Marta Li: This is helpful — let's recap. We'll provide payloads and infra constraints by Thursday. Redwood will send pilot SOW, SOC2, retention policies, and sample billing spreadsheet. We'll schedule benchmark next week. Does that match everyone?
[10:44] Sofia Ruiz: Yes.
[10:45] Connor Hale: Yep.
[10:46] Evan Brooks: Perfect — we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites. Thanks all.
[10:52] Marta Li: Thanks.
[10:54] (call ends)
